supply_chain_view.thesis: AI data center bottlenecks are migrating from accelerator availability alone into the full AI factory stack: advanced-node wafers, HBM and server DRAM, 2.5D/3D packaging, probe and inspection, CPO optical-engine yield, 1.6T optics, 800V HVDC power, grid interconnects, transformers, switchgear, and liquid cooling.
supply_chain_view.strict_score_implication: Microsoft and Alphabet confirm rapid AI infrastructure monetization, while Lam Research and FormFactor confirm operating leverage in equipment and test. Alphabet and Meta also show rising free-cash-flow pressure, and the July 30 earnings gaps remain poor entries. Structural bottleneck power does not remove capital-efficiency, valuation, trend, or entry risk.
bottleneck_migration: Compute remains scarce, but rack and site integration increasingly govern deployment speed.
HBM and server DRAM stay tight through 2027, while NAND supply can loosen in the second half of 2027.
Networking moves from 800G pluggables toward 1.6T, AECs, optical DSPs, silicon photonics, CPO, and NPO; optical-engine yield and advanced packaging now govern the ramp.
Power and cooling become first-order constraints as rack density rises and 800V HVDC architectures begin deployment.
Grid interconnection can take longer than the two-to-three-year data center construction cycle.

layers.score_adjustment: This is the most persistent two-year bottleneck, but leading public equities are already too large for credible 10x math.

methodology: Start with estimated AI data-center bottlenecks through July 2028.
Require direct exposure to yield, test, packaging, connectivity, power, or rack deployment constraints.
Compare the latest GAAP net income with the year-ago period and reject low-quality accounting gains.
Require market-cap headroom, filing-backed revenue, and a credible path to operating leverage.
Treat 10x as a scenario, not a forecast, target, or guaranteed return.
